question: Can one exact guided signal start a quiet localized counter orbit in an initially motionless, prepared remainder apparatus?
claim: Finite activation of a local oscillator by an ordinary signal, if the registered criteria pass. The remainder apparatus is prepared in advance; this is not creation from vacuum, a physical particle, a photon or a thermodynamic time arrow.
geometry: c=L//2. Exact +X guide at y=z=c on primary0/companion14. Center=(c,c+1,c), channel2, initially(a,b)=(0,0). Full336-triple region comprises this node and its six face neighbors. The other five outgoing recipients all start at the registered halo remainder. Every other regional triple is background(0,0,2), except the center's registered remainder. Packet origin=(c-18,c,c). No patches may overwrite conflicting assignments.

Record all six donor terms, before/after triples and exact C kind/quotient. A local transition with no input contact does not count as signal activation.

pair_acceptance: Complete initial rest and source-footprint equivalence; source-off entire board stationary throughout80updates; valid incoming templates; native first center activation with nonzero input and C; all late quiet-orbit conditions; full-state forward/inverse verification; strict initial causal margin and no active boundary contact.
